title: Dedicated tiers (draft): Standard / Plus / Premium
content:
Doc purpose
- Working draft of tier definitions for Redwood Dedicated: Standard / Plus / Premium.
- Intended audience: Product + SRE + Infra + Finance + Sales Enablement.
- Goal: converge on what we sell + what we can actually guarantee (and how we operationalize it) with minimal bespoke terms.

Status + what’s changing
- This is NOT contract language. It’s a product definition draft.
- Inputs still in flux: (a) canonical throughput metric semantics, (b) regional GPU supply constraints, (c) shape catalog + benchmark variance by model/context, (d) error budget policy + remedy hooks.

Definitions (shared)
1) “Dedicated deployment”
- A customer-isolated pool of capacity (one or more nodes) serving a specific configured model family/version (as defined in control plane config) with Redwood-managed orchestration and routing.
- Primary unit for guarantees: per Dedicated deployment (not per request route), unless explicitly noted.

2) “Committed throughput” (the floor)
- The minimum sustained throughput Redwood commits to provide for a Dedicated deployment under stated conditions.
- Expressed as tokens/sec (preferred) for generation and embeddings/sec (or tokens/sec equivalent) for embedding workloads.
- Committed throughput is tied to: (a) tier, (b) shape, (c) model/version class, (d) max context configuration.

3) “Burst throughput”
- Temporary additional throughput above the committed floor, subject to availability and burst policy.
- Burst can come from: (a) headroom on the customer’s dedicated pool, (b) tier-eligible shared burst pools in-region.

4) “Measurement window” (placeholder)
- Proposed working definition (needs SRE sign-off): measured over rolling 15-minute windows, evaluated continuously, reported as p50 and p95 tokens/sec; SLO evaluated on p95.
- We need one canonical definition in the SRE SLO doc; tiers should reference it rather than fork it.

5) “Customer-ready conditions” (when the guarantee applies)
- Deployment is in steady state: warm, healthy, and not in initial provisioning/warmup.
- Customer sends requests that conform to supported request shape constraints (see exclusions).
- Customer is not self-throttling below the committed floor (e.g., client-side QPS cap, concurrency cap, or low offered load).


Tier overview (one-paragraph positioning)
Standard
- Predictable single-region Dedicated capacity with a throughput floor on the provisioned shape; best-effort burst; standard support response.
Plus
- Higher committed throughput per $ (relative to Standard) via higher-utilization assumptions + access to managed burst pools; best-effort regional failover posture; faster support response and more proactive monitoring.
Premium
- Highest assurance: explicit headroom targets, warm standby / rapid replacement posture, priority handling during fleet contention, and contractual-ready SLO reporting + escalation. Designed for regulated / mission-critical workloads.


Entitlements matrix (draft)
NOTE: Numbers below are placeholders for product definition; actual floors come from Tier x Shape x Model perf profiles.

A) Throughput commitment (floor)
- Standard: Committed throughput = “Shape baseline” (per perf profile) with minimal additional headroom. SLO target: 99.0% of eligible 15-min windows meet/exceed floor.
- Plus: Committed throughput = “Shape baseline” with additional headroom and/or optimized routing/admission settings. SLO target: 99.5% of eligible 15-min windows meet/exceed floor.
- Premium: Committed throughput = “Shape baseline” with explicit N+1 / spare capacity posture depending on shape size + region. SLO target: 99.9% of eligible 15-min windows meet/exceed floor.

B) Burst policy
- Standard:
  - Included burst: none explicitly included; best-effort burst allowed if spare exists on the dedicated pool.
  - Burst sources: same pool only.
  - Burst cap: up to +20% above floor for short periods (guidance), no guarantee.
  - Billing: burst usage metered but not separately billable in v1 unless Finance wants explicit line item; TBD.
- Plus:
  - Included burst: up to +30% above committed floor for up to 2 hours/day (aggregate), subject to shared burst pool availability.
  - Burst sources: dedicated pool + shared in-region burst pool.
  - Burst behavior under contention: Plus requests get priority over Standard for burst pool, but do not preempt Premium.
  - Billing: over included burst billed at burst rate (needs metering event alignment).
- Premium:
  - Included burst: up to +50% above committed floor for up to 6 hours/day (aggregate), with higher availability target for burst pool access.
  - Burst sources: dedicated pool + shared in-region burst pool + (option) reserved surge capacity on premium-only pool.
  - Billing: over included burst billed at burst rate; option for pre-purchased surge add-on (sales package) TBD.

C) Failover expectations (availability posture)
- Standard:
  - Single-region only.
  - Hardware failures handled with best-effort replacement within business hours; no contractual RTO/RPO.
  - During node replacement, throughput may drop below floor; counted as SLO-impacting if within eligible conditions (needs SRE policy detail).
- Plus:
  - Primary region + best-effort failover to secondary region (if customer opts in + has networking/data egress approval).
  - Failover mode: “degraded service” allowed (higher latency, possibly lower throughput) but should preserve partial capacity.
  - Target operational objective (not a guarantee yet): begin failover within 60 minutes of confirmed capacity incident.
- Premium:
  - Two supported modes:
    1) Single-region with “rapid replacement” posture (priority swap + warm spares)
    2) Dual-region with warm standby (customer chooses)
  - Target operational objective (candidate): begin failover within 15 minutes of confirmed capacity incident; achieve stable degraded service within 30 minutes.
  - Premium gets priority in regional rebalancing during fleet contention.

D) Support + response targets
- Standard:
  - Support channel: standard support portal.
  - Initial response target: 4 business hours.
  - Escalation: on-call SRE engagement during business hours for confirmed platform-side incidents.
- Plus:
  - Support channel: support portal + shared Slack/Connect channel (optional for enterprise accounts).
  - Initial response target: 1 hour (business hours) / 4 hours (off hours).
  - Escalation: on-call SRE engagement for confirmed SLO-impacting incidents.
- Premium:
  - Support channel: named escalation path + optional 24/7 paging for SEV-1.
  - Initial response target: 15 minutes for SEV-1 / 1 hour for SEV-2, 24/7.
  - Proactive comms: incident updates every 30 minutes for SEV-1 until mitigated; post-incident RCA within 5 business days.

E) Observability + reporting
- Standard:
  - Console visibility: current utilization, basic throughput charts, last 24h.
  - Monthly SLO summary available on request.
- Plus:
  - Console visibility: tier-aware SLO widget, 7–30 day retention, per-model breakdown.
  - Monthly SLO summary delivered automatically (email/console export).
- Premium:
  - Console visibility: advanced SLO reporting + export API + incident timeline integration.
  - Quarterly review: capacity + performance review with Solutions + SRE (optional but bundled in packaging).


How committed throughput is set (practical product rule)
- We do NOT promise a single number per tier independent of shape/model. We promise:
  1) a floor derived from Redwood’s perf profile for (shape, model/version, context cap, decoding config), and
  2) that Redwood will provision/operate the deployment so that the measured throughput meets that floor under eligible conditions.
- Customer-facing quoting artifact should include:
  - chosen tier
  - region(s)
  - shape
  - model/version pin
  - max context (and any special decoding settings)
  - committed throughput floor number(s)


Supported workloads / constraints (draft; align with SRE/Infra)
- Supported request patterns (eligible for guarantee):
  - streaming or non-streaming generation requests with standard SDK parameters
  - embeddings requests within max batch size guidance
- Constraints that must be explicitly configured / enforced:
  - max context length per deployment (e.g., 8k/16k/32k depending on shape + model)
  - max output tokens / max new tokens
  - concurrency limits consistent with shape guidance
  - any enforced decoding knobs that materially change throughput (e.g., speculative decoding on/off)


Exclusions (things that will invalidate or pause SLO evaluation)
These are the main “don’t get gamed / don’t create impossible ops burden” items.
- Customer-offered load below the floor:
  - If the customer sends insufficient traffic (low concurrency/QPS) such that the deployment is not demand-saturated, then observed tokens/sec may be below the floor and should not count as an SLO miss.
- Customer-side throttling or backpressure:
  - Client rate limits, concurrency caps, or network constraints causing low effective throughput.
- Unsupported model/version or unpinned model behavior:
  - If customer uses an unapproved model, or changes model version without Redwood perf profile coverage, the floor is not valid.
- Request shapes outside documented bounds:
  - Context length above configured max
  - Output lengths consistently above recommended max
  - Extremely skewed prompt distributions that materially differ from sizing assumptions (to be defined carefully; avoid subjective language)
- Abuse / misuse patterns:
  - Intentional traffic patterns to inflate measurement noise (e.g., high churn of tiny requests that create overhead) if outside published guidance.
- Planned maintenance windows (Premium may have stricter change control):
  - Maintenance communicated in advance; windows excluded from SLO evaluation.


Admission control + overload behavior (tier semantics)
- Standard:
  - When saturated, requests may see increased queueing and higher tail latency; Redwood may shed excess load to protect fleet stability.
  - No guarantee that burst is available.
- Plus:
  - When saturated, admission control prioritizes maintaining the committed floor; overflow can be routed to burst pool if available.
  - Shedding policy should protect committed traffic first; burst traffic is the first to be shed.
- Premium:
  - Strongest protection: Premium committed traffic takes precedence during contention; premium can utilize reserved surge capacity if configured.
  - Goal: preserve both floor + reasonable tail latency; if a tradeoff is necessary, prioritize maintaining the throughput floor.


Customer-facing language draft (non-legal, for docs/enablement)
- Standard: “Dedicated capacity with a defined throughput floor on your selected hardware shape, measured by Redwood’s Dedicated throughput SLO methodology. Best-effort burst on available headroom.”
- Plus: “Higher assurance Dedicated capacity with a throughput floor plus included burst and best-effort failover options. Faster support response and tier-prioritized handling during contention.”
- Premium: “Mission-critical Dedicated capacity with the strongest throughput assurance, priority handling, and premium escalation. Includes the most complete SLO reporting, proactive incident communications, and optional warm standby/failover posture.”


Remedies / credits (placeholder; needs Finance + Legal)
- Standard: no automatic credits; handle case-by-case.
- Plus: service credits for verified SLO misses beyond error budget threshold, capped monthly (candidate: 10% of monthly fee). TBD.
- Premium: service credits with clearer schedule + faster dispute window; higher cap (candidate: 25% of monthly fee). TBD.


Open questions / decisions needed
1) Metric definition (tokens/sec)
- Do we define throughput as output tokens/sec, total tokens/sec (input+output), or a weighted measure?
- How do we normalize across streaming vs non-streaming? (Recent streaming double-counting bug is a warning.)
- Owner: Sean Gallagher (SRE). Target: align with ADR + SRE SLO doc.

2) Per-deployment vs per-route
- This doc assumes per-deployment. If we allow multiple routes/models on one deployment, do we need allocation rules?
- Proposal: v1 limit Dedicated deployments to a single pinned model/version (or a Redwood-defined compatible set) to keep guarantees sane.

3) Burst inclusions
- Are the included burst hours/day the right packaging lever, or should we sell burst as a separate add-on?
- Finance preference seems to be: make burst visible and billable beyond included to avoid margin surprises.

4) Failover packaging
- What is realistically supportable in regions with heterogeneous GPU supply?
- Is “Plus best-effort failover” too hand-wavy for sales? If yes, limit Plus to “priority replacement” instead of cross-region failover.

5) Support targets
- Confirm with Support/CS what we can staff for 15-minute SEV-1 response (Premium) and what qualifies as SEV-1.

6) Shape catalog alignment
- Need a single canonical mapping: Tier -> allowed shapes (per region) + allowed model/context combos.
- Owner: Irene Choi / Vanessa Ortiz. Output: quoting-friendly table + lead-time guidance.


Next steps (proposed)
- 03/29: cross-functional review meeting (Product + SRE + Infra + Finance + Enablement) to lock:
  - tier names and entitlements (esp. burst + failover posture)
  - support response targets
  - what becomes hard commitment vs “operational objective”
- Early April: convert this draft into:
  - Confluence PRD section update
  - Sales cheat sheet content
  - customer-facing docs draft (non-legal) + legal-reviewed SLO language (separate)

Notes to self (Lauren)
- Keep tiers simple enough that Sales can quote without bespoke exceptions.
- Avoid guaranteeing things that require per-account custom ops (e.g., bespoke multi-region setups) unless Premium-only and priced accordingly.
- Make sure we explicitly state the “eligible conditions” so SLO doesn’t get gamed and so support triage is deterministic.
